common_premise: Fixed R; valid current global/temp/map/player objects and registries. These are personally read complete source units and finite Settings consumers. Ordinary positive random bounds have separate static contract; native samples, map transfers, battles, messages and save roundtrip were not executed. WP02 configuration-definition children are joined only to the named consumers here, not to whole roaming/Phone/domain acceptance.

facts.meaning: pbRoamingAreas rereads ROAMING_SPECIES[index], returning its truthy sixth element unchanged; absent entry or false/nil sixth element returns the common ROAMING_AREAS object, with no clone or merge. Default common map keys are ordered5,21,28,31,39,41,44,47,66,69, each adjacency lists the other nine in that order. LATIAS30/switch53/method0/BGM Battle roaming and LATIOS identical except species use common graph; KYOGRE40/switch54/method2/nilBGM uses graph2:[21,31],21:[2,31,69],31:[2,21,69],69:[21,31]; ENTEI40/switch55/method1 has omitted BGM/graph and uses common graph.
facts.control: A supplied empty graph is truthy and replaces common graph; missing roamer index still returns common graph in this helper, though callers may independently require a data tuple. Switch numbers are IDs, not booleans or species availability guarantees.
facts.failure_prefix: Helper performs no write. Invalid plugin tuple/graph type may fail before callers can choose keys; no normalization or arbitrary graph validation is supplied.
facts.open: Actual map existence/connectivity/name/region and species literal registry membership require their independently received records. No route distribution execution proof.

facts.meaning: pbRoamPokemon initializes roamPokemon=[] if nil, then only when roamPosition is nil creates{} and iterates current ROAMING_SPECIES length. Each existing species gets a random graph key even when its positive switch is currently off. It then iterates current length again invoking pbRoamPokemonOne. An existing hash, including empty{}, skips the initial placement pass. pbRandomRoam is an explicit other helper and returns when no position object exists; it does not gate switch/species itself.
facts.control: Species.exists? suppresses initial position for unknown species. Empty keys reaches rand(0) and indexing without a local guard in these two initial/random helpers; no native return/index failure is inferred. Config edits do not delete stale positional keys or recreate existing positions.
facts.failure_prefix: roamPokemon/roamPosition and earlier per-index placements commit before later failures. A failure in initialization or one move stops remaining indices; no rollback/ensure.
facts.open: Native zero-bound rand and indexing acceptance are separate unresolved obligations. Full dynamic Settings changes and all map consumers are not accepted.

facts.meaning: pbRoamPokemonOne reads tuple and exits for positive switchID whose game switch is false, then unknown species, then empty graph keys. If current position is absent it immediately stores a random graph key. Missing adjacency for current map returns retaining that placement. Otherwise copies adjacency entries, independently adds a random graph key on rand(32)==0, then if choices nonempty stores random chosen entry. Neighbors need not be graph keys or unique; helper does not deduplicate or check their existence.
facts.control: SwitchID<=0 bypasses switch guard. A current map with empty adjacency still has the 1/32 branch before the empty-choice test. on_enter_map skips movement when old positive map has a known nonnil name equal to current name; otherwise moves all then clears roamedAlready=false.
facts.failure_prefix: Initial placement can persist if later adjacency access/random operation fails. on_enter_map resets roamedAlready only after pbRoamPokemon returns normally; no ensure.
facts.open: Host RNG/native switch caller execution and map-transition handler ordering remain unobserved. Global switch defaults are separate source facts, not supplied by nonzeroID.

facts.meaning: on_wild_species_chosen first clears temp roamer index, then skips nil encounter/already-roamed/partner/PokeRadar and rand100<75. It scans current tuples, requiring species exists, enabled positive switch and roamPokemon[i]!=true. Missing position is assigned a random available graph key. Different map qualifies only with matching current region metadata and matching current map name. Method0 permits land/cave/water;1 land/cave;2 water;3 fishing;4 water/fishing; others false. It samples eligible tuples, writes roamEncounter and temp index, optionally nextBattleBGM only for nonempty BGM, forces single and overwrites encounter species/level.
facts.control: 25% is merely the preliminary random gate; no eligible tuple means unchanged encounter. Same actual map bypasses region/name-equivalence checks. The callback expects roamPokemon and roamPosition already initialized by the movement lifecycle. No BGM resets on nil/empty tuple BGM.
facts.failure_prefix: Temp index is cleared even on ordinary skip. Missing-map placement may persist before later candidate failure; selected global/temp/BGM/single writes occur before encounter writes. No rollback if subsequent handler fails.
facts.open: Earlier/later encounter callbacks, battle audio implementation and actual eligibility fixture values are only accepted under separately named contributions. No ordinary encounter always becomes a roamer.

facts.meaning: on_calling_wild_battle acts only when handled[0] is nil and global roamEncounter/tempindex exist; assignment of handled occurs after pbRoamingPokemonBattle returns. That method creates/stores a Pokemon when cached value is absent or not Pokemon, requests single and roamerFlees, calls WildBattle.start_core, stores sentineltrue on decision1 or4 and writes caught boolean(decision4), then clears global encounter, sets roamedAlreadytrue and clears tempindex before wild-end event. Return false only for2 or5. pbResetAllRoamers code resets sentineltrue only when roamPokemonCaught[i] is truthy, despite preceding comment describing defeated-without-caught; this is recorded as actual source condition, no new formal finding.
facts.control: Other decisions retain cached Pokemon object and its mutations. Caught array is lazily created by getter; roamer index itself is temp, while positions/cachedPokemon/caught/roamedAlready are Global fields. Priorhandledfalse also suppresses override, since only nil permits it.
facts.failure_prefix: Generated Pokemon can be stored before rule/battle failure. Decision sentinel and cleanup precede wild-end event; event failure leaves cleaned indices and prevents handled assignment. No ensure, rollback or automatic retry safety. NonPokemon pkmn argument may reach final pkmn.species_data access after preceding commits; no universal argument validity claim.
facts.open: Battle core, Pokemon inner serialization compatibility, on_wild_battle_end callbacks and comment-versus-formal full domain audit remain outside this finite contribution.

facts.meaning: Phone.initialize sets contacts[],rematch_variant0, copies PHONE_REMATCHES_POSSIBLE_FROM_BEGINNING(defaultfalse) once into @rematches_enabled, then initializes call timer0.0/refresh0. Global initializer constructs Phone.new. Static Phone.rematches_enabled getter/setter reads/writes the stored Global.phone property; later Settings edits do not update existing phones. refresh_ready_trainers returns immediately when disabled, otherwise at most once per distinct pbGetTimeNow.to_i value sets last_refresh first and visits visible trainer contacts not already rematch-ready. Nonpositive countdown resets to rand(20...40)*60, then subtracts1; ready sets flag1 then event A=false/B=true/maprefresh.
facts.control: Frame callback requires Pokegear and no menu/battle/message/forced-route/interpreter, so elapsed wall time does not automatically catch up countdown. The random range excludes40. Contact getters return only visible matching kind/type/name/start-version; setters can later enable rematches independently of original configuration.
facts.failure_prefix: Construction writes earlier fields before settings access. Refresh timestamp and earlier contacts can commit before later failure; setting ready flag precedes self-switch writes, with no rollback. Frame call timer subtracts Graphics.delta, independently of trainer readiness's one-per-second decrement.
facts.open: Actual on_frame_update cadence, Time/native Graphics.delta and all contact event execution remain unobserved; full migration/inner Phone native roundtrip not granted.

facts.meaning: Phone::Call.play calls start_message first, computes species/map substitutions, then rereads COLOR_PHONE_CALL_MESSAGES_BY_CONTACT_GENDER(defaulttrue) each call and only for trainer contacts. Known TrainerType gender0 gets \b,1 gets \r; unknown type/other gender/nontrainer/disabled get no prefix. It splits dialogue on literal \m, substitutes TN via _INTL(contact.name), TP/TE/TM computed strings, adds continuation marker except last, sends each pbMessage(prefix+message), then end_message. Incoming/outgoing common-event branches call pbCommonEvent instead of this play path; setting does not recolor their event messages.
facts.control: Generated trainer dialogue selects exact version then start-version then default data; ready flag1 is changed to2 while constructing battle request, before play. Encounter species display uses direct versioned Encounter.get and first four Land slots, then Cave then Water, not each_of_version or weighted runtime selection.
facts.failure_prefix: Opening message happens before data/colour lookup; any later lookup/substitution/display failure leaves earlier messages and possibly rematch_flag2. Closing message occurs only after all split segments; no ensure. Common-event false produces its separate diagnostic; failure does not route through colour play automatically.
facts.open: Actual Intl lookup/TrainerType gender literals/message native control parsing and common-event execution require their separate contracts; no pixel, translated-colour or complete Phone behavior approval.

facts.meaning: Global exposes phone and roaming fields; its initializer constructs Phone but roaming extension provides no field initializer, except caught getter lazily substitutes[]. Existing Global outer object save/load contract can retain these references and stored flags/timers; Settings copies are not recomputed by merely assigning a loaded Global. Contact hiding changes visible first, then trainer timers/flag/selfswitchA/maprefresh; add can restore/delete existing visible contact, push and reorder before a separate public registration message. These are explicit partial-commit objects, not transactionally rolled back user cancellations.
facts.control: Deprecated pbPhoneRegisterBattle returns false before add on can_add? failure or declined confirmation; accepted add persists before its public message. Full source reading does not certify the deprecated argument wrappers' universal correctness or undefined identifiers in uninvoked branches.
facts.failure_prefix: Global construction may fail after Phone creation on later regionalDex/DayCare construction. Save assignment and direct-write failure behavior is only the separately received outer SaveData contract; no inner serialization/native reload validation has occurred.
facts.open: All conversion/migration treatment of inner phone/roamer state, graph aliasing after Marshal, every deprecated wrapper and downstream UI/native/event behavior remain independently scoped. No new finding/context/vote.

persistence: Outer Global registration/load was independently read earlier. This package supplies exact producer and consumer mutations in its newly read complete files, not a new native save/reload execution claim or whole domain migration acceptance.
remaining: Nine original lexical candidates received locally; complete dynamic/transitive consumer denominator remains unfrozen. Personal sourceFULL credit remains distinct from finite manual fact coverage.
